final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position to match the existing record. That reframing is useful but not curative. The key distinction is that a caveated operational certification rationale may be supportable as a business decision, but compliance under the stated policy requires evidence that the material weakness for the named launch use case was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. That predicate remains unmet on the available record. Because the unresolved issue is an actual policy condition rather than a disclosure nuance that can be cured by caveated wording alone, the case remains noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the tax filing assistant limitation was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering the named use case and the 1.4-point gap.
The affected segment is named in two tax-season partner commitments, which supports materiality under the policy text.
Legal review remains open, so the disclosure predicate is still unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and monitoring-oriented public guidance do not satisfy the internal disclosure requirement on their own.
